notation_and_corrections: Use E for notebook input rows; supplied comparison's X=E. Lower full-width U_K,i is relabeled W_i^K, while upper latent map remains U_K,i.
All row-oriented dimensions and transposes checked. The comparisons produce one 1-by-n score row, not one scalar.
Content score scaling remains sqrt(d_h) after absorption, not sqrt(r). Full positional score scaling is sqrt(d_h+d_R).
Caching X halves KV scalar count only when D=H*d_h and both key/value widths equal d_h in this bias-free, position-free comparison.
Operation counts compare reconstructing keys from C with transforming one query; they are not a performance claim against already-cached conventional MHA.
The token-11 diagram processes the current token including itself; its output contributes to following-token prediction.
About 400 GB in the 100k-token example can denote stored history and approximate history reads per new query; the allocation increase is about 4 MB.
Nonlinear latent normalization cannot be absorbed into a fixed matrix; only adjacent linear maps are regrouped.
